hints: For each customer, find the most expensive remaining ticket price no greater than their limit.
A sorted multiset can find that predecessor value while keeping duplicate ticket copies separate.
Remove exactly one ticket when sold; print -1 when no eligible ticket exists.
analogy: Take the closest price from below the customer's budget, then remove that one ticket from the shelf.
example: Tickets 3,5,7 and limit 6: sell 5; a later limit 4 can still buy 3.
algorithm: Store ticket prices in a multiset. For each limit t, locate the greatest element <=t, print and erase one occurrence; if none exists print -1.
correctness: The chosen ticket is the highest affordable available price by the predecessor search, and erasing one occurrence enforces that each ticket is sold at most once.
complexity: O((n+m) log n) time and O(n) space.
